payload.reason: Both proposals agree on how the work is split up. Each ledger finish line gets its own package under tests/acceptance/. The ten E-001/E-002 Go bodies are committed verbatim. A shared harness that imports only the standard library builds ./cmd/hband and drives it over HTTP. A DevTools driver that imports only the standard library goes inside internal/testutil/headless. TestBrowserSkipEndsTheCallingTest moves to a child process. The Python-to-Go mapping is a Go table that a test checks. Where the proposals differ, this design picks against the tree as measured and against the two spikes. One gap is named here: the six Python ledger bodies (epics 41-44) were not read at design time. This stage has only Read, Glob and Grep, and the ledger may only be read through a mode=ro SELECT. The build-check survey (surveys#198) recorded approximate assertion counts for them, not the assertions themselves, and C4 depends on the assertions. That survey should have quoted them. The design does not stop for this, because porting is mechanical once the bodies are read. The builder's first step is that read in place. The mapping checker then makes it impossible to drop an assertion without the per-source count going red. The critique has to re-read the bodies in place and compare the recorded sha256 editions (lessons #951, #861).
payload.selection_rationale:
Practice is the core. It matches how the tree is already shaped. TestBinary's build, start, 'listening addr=' wait and Host-rewrite pattern (cmd/hband/main_test.go) is package-main test code, so it has to be re-expressed in an importable package. headless.Browser is already the one CHROME_BIN gate, so Open(t) calls Browser itself and takes no path parameter, and the rule is then structurally impossible to bypass. Shot already chose os.MkdirTemp over t.TempDir for Windows cleanup, and the harness copies that. config.Load gives plain hband_sid cookies on a loopback-http base (SecureCookies only for https; cookieName adds __Host- only then). So Chrome can sign itself in through fakegithub with no Fetch bridge and no cookie injection. That also keeps the harness clear of the fitness rule 'every cookie is written by the one cookie helper', which forbids http.Cookie literals. Crossdomain's Network.setCookie would have needed one more CDP method and a cookie read from the jar, and neither spike proved it.

Three pieces come from crossdomain. (1) Build and Start are separate calls, so the loopback retry and the later launcher reuse one binary. (2) The disposition kinds and the two-way `// ported:<ID>` tags. (3) Per-source editions (sha256), which are the only way the critique and SC-043 can prove the table was made from the bodies they are about to delete. Crossdomain's subtest layout for the browser checks is rejected, because it would run E-004 line 2's HTTP assertions on loopback http and not on the production https/__Host- path. Practice's split keeps that fidelity at the cost of one more start, about 3 s.

Both proposals wanted C5 to be builder-run evidence that is not committed. That is overridden. A case needs a check that a machine can run unattended, and E-009 line 5 covers only E-001, E-003 and E-006, and is planted only at epic-finish time. So a build-tagged test commits the seven overlay-trigger breaks, one or more per epic. Everything browser-related rests on measurements, not argument. Spike 207 drove Chrome 158 from Go using only the standard library, at 360 and 400 px, with no Origin header and a clean Browser.close, in 0.5-0.9 s over 5 of 5 runs. Spike 2 read scrollWidth 360/400/985 and the exact toggle sequence on hband pages. Spike 3 measured all 15 non-browser bodies passing at HEAD. Practice raised over_engineering_flag, and it is honoured: no automation library, no specification/driver layering, four CDP verbs, and the ten Go bodies are not rewritten. Crossdomain's go/parser reconciliation is the one addition kept over that flag, because SC-043 deletes the Python on its word.

components.name: program harness (new, test-only)
components.responsibility:
T is the narrow interface {Helper(); Fatalf(string, ...any); Logf(string, ...any); Cleanup(func())}. testing.TB satisfies it. Fatalf must not return. Build(t T) string. The go tool is exec.LookPath("go"), falling back to filepath.Join(runtime.GOROOT(),"bin","go[.exe]"). It runs `go build -buildvcs=false -o /hband[.exe] github.com/sshubham2/hband/cmd/hband` with Env = os.Environ()+CGO_ENABLED=0, untouched otherwise, so a GOFLAGS -overlay (E-009 lines 4/5, the breaks test) reaches it. Dir is left unset, because the caller's package dir is inside the module. A failure calls Fatalf with the combined output. Cleanup removes the folder: 10 tries 200 ms apart, logged and never fatal. Start(t T, bin string, o Options) *Program does five things. (1) It starts fakegithub.New("cid", testSecret, base+"/auth/github/callback") and registers Close. (2) It makes the data dir and working dir with os.MkdirTemp, never t.TempDir and never inside the repository. (3) It builds the child env: os.Environ() with every name whose upper-cased form starts HBAND_ removed, plus HBAND_ADDR, HBAND_BASE_URL, HBAND_DATA_DIR, HBAND_OWNER_GITHUB_ID=4242, HBAND_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID=cid, HBAND_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET=testSecret, HBAND_GITHUB_URL=HBAND_GITHUB_API_URL=fake.URL(), HBAND_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES=26214400 and HBAND_TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1, then o.Env overrides. (4) It waits up to 30 s for `listening addr=(\S+)`. A process that exits first calls Fatalf naming its exit code and the log tail. This is the path line 4's exit-3 overlay takes, so every port fails. (5) It GETs /healthz and requires 200, which is the serve_show_all.py readiness assertion. There are two modes. The default is HBAND_ADDR=127.0.0.1:0 with base https://hband.test, and the bound address is read from the log, so there is no port race and 8080 is never used. Loopback (o.Loopback, or o.Port>0) uses base http://127.0.0.1:

with HBAND_ADDR=127.0.0.1:

. P comes from the package var pickPort (listen on :0, then close) unless o.Port is fixed. In picked mode only, an exit with code 1 before listening is retried up to 3 attempts in total, with a fresh port and fake.SetRedirectURI. Any other exit code calls Fatalf at once. Cleanup is LIFO: kill the process and wait (WaitDelay 5 s), close the fake, then remove the folders with logged retries.
components.key_interactions: It imports only the standard library and internal/testutil/fakegithub (architecture rule 2; E-009 line 4's link-none check). It is used by the six ports, the breaks test and the later seeded launcher, which supplies its own T. It reads os.Environ only to pass it through. It never reads CHROME_BIN or any browser variable.

components.name: Visitor (the harness's HTTP client)
components.responsibility:
p.Anonymous() and p.SignIn(t, fakegithub.User) return *Visitor, which is a cookie-jar client. p.Owner(t) is SignIn as {ID:4242, Login:"owner"}. SignIn calls p.Fake.SetUser(u), GETs /auth/github/login?next=/ and follows the redirect chain through the fake. It calls Fatalf unless it lands with 200 and the jar holds the session cookie for Base, whatever its __Host- prefix.

The transport is its own &http.Transport{Proxy: nil}. In default mode it is wrapped in a rewrite that sends host hband.test to http://<Addr> and sets resp.Request back to the original, as cmd/hband's rewrite does, so the jar keeps Secure cookies. Requests to any other host pass straight through. The client timeout is 30 s.

Methods: Get(t, path) Page follows redirects and records the final URL. Post(t, path, url.Values) Page and Upload(t, path, fields map[string]string, fileField, fileName string, data []byte) Page never follow, and return the Location header. Publish(t, slug, title, html) is the owner's Upload to POST /admin/reports with the fields TestBinary posts (status published) and requires a 303. Page is {Status int; Header http.Header; Body string; Location string; URL string}. A transport error calls Fatalf with the method and path. Status and body checks belong to the calling test, so the failure names the epic's own assertion.
components.key_interactions: Go requests carry neither Origin nor Sec-Fetch-Site, which CrossOriginProtection lets through, as TestBinary already relies on. It never constructs an http.Cookie literal (fitness rule 'every cookie is written by the one cookie helper').

components.name: headless DevTools driver (grows the helper)
components.responsibility:
Open(t testing.TB) *Tab calls Browser(t) first. If Browser returns "" (a recorder TB), Open returns nil and starts nothing. A real *testing.T has already been ended by Skip, with Browser's message naming CHROME_BIN.

It starts exactly the path Browser returned: --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-first-run --no-default-browser-check --disable-extensions --no-proxy-server --remote-debugging-port=0 --user-data-dir=<os.MkdirTemp profile> about:blank. It polls <profile>/DevToolsActivePort for up to 15 s (first line = port). If the process exits first, or the 15 s run out, it kills the process and calls Fatalf. It GETs http://127.0.0.1:<port>/json/list with a client whose Proxy is nil and takes the first target of type page.

The WebSocket client is a hand-written RFC 6455 client, in devtools_ws.go. It sends no Origin header. Its key is 16 random bytes, and it verifies Sec-WebSocket-Accept = base64(sha1(key+GUID)). Client frames are masked. It reads 7-, 16- and 64-bit lengths and continuation frames, answers pings with pongs, and stops on close. One reader goroutine routes replies by id and keeps events. After connecting, Open calls Page.enable.

Tab methods:
- Call(method string, params any) json.RawMessage fails the test after 30 s or on a protocol error, naming the method.
- Viewport(w, h int, mobile bool) sends Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride with deviceScaleFactor 2 for mobile and 1 otherwise.
- Navigate(url) clears the load events it has kept, calls Page.navigate, fails on errorText, and waits up to 30 s for Page.loadEventFired.
- Eval(expr string, out any) sends Runtime.evaluate with returnByValue and awaitPromise, fails on exceptionDetails with its text, and unmarshals result.value.

Its Cleanup sends Browser.close, waits up to 10 s for exit, kills if needed, then calls removeLoud(profile). It reads no environment (architecture rule 3). The builder updates headless.go's package comment, which today says there is no DevTools client.
components.key_interactions: This is the only new place in the repository that starts a browser, and it sits beside Shot. Shot and Count are unchanged for TestReportScriptsNeverRun. Acceptance tests reach a browser only through Open (architecture rule 4).

With CHROME_BIN unset, empty, naming a folder, or naming an empty file called msedge.exe, Open returns nil, the recorder records a skip naming CHROME_BIN, and no process is started. components.name: E-003, E-004 line 1, E-005 and E-006 ports
components.responsibility:
There is one package per Python body, each a single top-level test: e003_1_sign_in_and_vote (TestE003SignInAndVote), e004_1_comments_and_replies (TestE004CommentsAndReplies), e005_1_private_feedback (TestE005PrivateFeedback), e006_1_removal_and_placeholders (TestE006RemovalAndPlaceholders) and e006_2_blocking_and_unblocking (TestE006BlockingAndUnblocking).

The porting rule:
- Every assert site of the unittest method becomes one Go check at the same point, with t.Fatalf, because unittest stops at the first failure.
- A self.subTest becomes t.Run.
- An assertion inside a Python helper (for example a press helper's status check) is ported once into the matching Go helper, with its tag there and Via naming the test.
- Each check carries `// ported:<ID>`.

All of them drive the program through program.Build, Start (the default https://hband.test base), Owner, SignIn, Get, Post and Upload. They follow the pins already known: #963 for E-005 (feedback-\d+ ids, /admin/feedback/<n>/reply, /reports/<slug>/feedback, one 'body' field), and the route table for E-006 (/admin/comments/{n}/remove, /admin/users/{u}/block|unblock, /admin/blocked). The Python stand-in GitHub becomes fakegithub, and each fake-side check becomes an Amended row saying fakegithub refuses the same request.

components.name: assertion mapping and its checker (tooling)
components.key_interactions: This is the record that lets SC-043 delete the Python. It never needs the Python files to exist. Its test names carry no E00x, so E-009 lines 4 and 5 do not treat it as an acceptance test. It is tooling the build checks, not prose.

components.name: broken-behaviour check (build-tagged)
components.key_interactions: This settles C5 for every epic with a check a machine can run. E-009 line 5 stays the engine's own independent check of E-001, E-003 and E-006. If a ledger body does not fail under its break, the builder names another test of that epic that does, and says so.

key_decisions.decision: Each ledger finish line gets its own Go package at tests/acceptance/<line name>/<line name>_test.go. Top-level names carry the epic key (TestE00N<What>). No test outside tests/acceptance carries E00[1-6] (architecture rule 5).
key_decisions.rationale: E-009 lines 4 and 5 find acceptance tests by the E00N key and need them outside the product's packages. One package per line keeps the ten Go bodies' private helpers from colliding, and each mapping row then traces to exactly one old body.

key_decisions.decision: The ten E-001/E-002 ledger Go bodies are committed verbatim at their planted paths. They are amended only where E-009 line 4 or 5 forces it, and each amendment is marked `// SC-042:` and has an Amended row. The checker proves each unamended body's sha256 equals its ledger edition.
key_decisions.rationale: They are the approved finish lines and pass at HEAD (spike 3). Rewriting them on the harness could only drift. With the edition check, 'verbatim' is a fact a machine verifies rather than a claim.

key_decisions.decision: A shared harness, internal/testutil/program, imports only the standard library. It has separate Build and Start calls. Build passes os.Environ() through untouched and uses -buildvcs=false. Every folder comes from os.MkdirTemp. The default base is https://hband.test on 127.0.0.1:0 through a Host rewrite. Loopback http on a picked port is the browser's mode, retried only on exit code 1 before listening. Readiness is 'listening addr=' plus /healthz 200.
key_decisions.rationale: cmd/hband's helpers are package-main test code and cannot be imported. Passing the environment through is what lets the overlays of line 4, line 5 and the breaks test reach the build. Port 0 removes the port race and never touches 8080. The https base exercises the production __Host- cookie path that TestBinary and the ledger bodies use. MkdirTemp follows Shot's measured Windows lesson. Proxy: nil makes line 4's dead proxies inert for the tests' own clients.

key_decisions.decision: The E-004 browser checks get a stdlib-only DevTools driver inside internal/testutil/headless. Open(t) takes no path and calls Browser itself. It uses four verbs: Call, Viewport, Navigate and Eval. It adds no dependency.
key_decisions.rationale: The BROWSER RULE, Q-034 and Q-035 (a person) require the helper and CHROME_BIN only. With no path parameter, no caller can hand Open anything but CHROME_BIN's value. Shot's command line cannot go below about 492 px or click (#940, run_finish_e004_2.py L25), and spike 207 measured this exact client at 360/400 px. Only golang.org/x/oauth2 and modernc.org/sqlite are allowed as dependencies. This departs from the stale '[testing] … --screenshot … Edge here … HBAND_TEST_BROWSER' stack line, which Q-035 retired. It is declared in stack_chosen.

key_decisions.decision: Chrome signs itself in through fakegithub on an http://127.0.0.1:<port> base. There is no DevTools Fetch bridge and no Network.setCookie.
key_decisions.rationale: SecureCookies is false and cookieName drops __Host- on a loopback-http base, so a real OAuth round trip in Chrome leaves a plain hband_sid. This removes the Python's untested request-interception bridge, needs no fifth CDP verb, and keeps the harness clear of the http.Cookie-literal fitness rule. If Chrome lands signed out, the added check (location is Branch, details.reply present) goes red, and the fallback is Network.setCookie with the jar's cookie. The cost: the signed-in look runs with a non-Secure cookie. The https cookie path stays covered over HTTP, and Q-006 stays open.

key_decisions.decision: test_e004_2's single unittest method becomes two Go tests. TestE004DeepThreadsAndBranchPages runs the HTTP part, with no browser, on the https base. TestE004FoldAndFitInBrowser runs the browser part on loopback. Every other port is one test, with t.Fatalf at each assertion. The look's six width checks are t.Errorf, so all six are measured as the Python collected them.
key_decisions.rationale: As one test it would skip whole without CHROME_BIN, and C1 would lose its non-browser assertions. Running the HTTP part on loopback would weaken it to the non-production cookie path. The error semantics follow each source: unittest stops at the first failure, while look() records every width before failing.

key_decisions.decision: The C4 mapping is a Go table checked by TestPortedAssertionsHaveAGoTest. It records per-source assertion counts and editions, five dispositions (Ported, Verbatim, Helper, Amended, Superseded), and two-way `// ported:<ID>` tags, which are checked with go/parser against function spans.
key_decisions.rationale: Prose is not slice work and drifts silently. Counts catch a dropped assertion. Tags tie each row to the exact function that makes the check. Editions let the critique and SC-043 prove, by an in-place SELECT, that the table was made from the bodies being deleted. That totality step cannot run inside go test, because tests must not read the ledger. Every deliberate change, such as the msedge browser list, is declared as Amended rather than silently left out.

key_decisions.decision: C5 is a committed, build-tagged test (sc042breaks) with seven overlay-trigger breaks, at least one per epic. Each break has an as-is pass, a broken fail, and a mark file that tells 'break never met' apart from 'break missed'. It overrides both proposals, which wanted builder-run evidence that is not committed.
key_decisions.rationale: A case needs a check a machine can run unattended. E-009 line 5 samples only E-001, E-003 and E-006 and is planted only at epic finish. Triggers ride the real binary through GOFLAGS -overlay, exactly as line 5 does, so no product source changes. A break of the client-side toggle (thread.js) is not included: overlays carry Go files, and the toggle readings are exact values that a no-op handler already fails.

key_decisions.decision: TestBrowserSkipEndsTheCallingTest runs its real-skip check in a child of the test binary, gated by HBAND_TEST_SKIP_CALLER=1.
key_decisions.rationale: As written, its 'caller' subtest ends as SKIP naming CHROME_BIN even when CHROME_BIN is Chrome. That fails E-009 line 2, and with it C2, whatever the ports do. Line 2's own comment prescribes the child-process form.

key_decisions.decision: Acceptance packages use no t.Parallel. In every test a break samples, the guarded write comes after at least one earlier sign-in round trip.
key_decisions.rationale: TestConcurrentVotesNoBusy already flakes under whole-suite load (#987, Q-030 open), and the acceptance packages add about 16 builds and starts. The breaks install their trigger on a 10 ms poll once the table exists. Making the guarded write the first request could beat the trigger, and the mark file would then show the break was never met.

contracts.name: program.Build(t T) string
contracts.error_cases: No go tool on PATH or under GOROOT: Fatalf. go build exits non-zero, including an overlay in GOFLAGS that does not compile: Fatalf with the combined output. Folder removal failure: Logf only.
contracts.notes: `go build -buildvcs=false -o <MkdirTemp>/hband[.exe] github.com/sshubham2/hband/cmd/hband`, with Env = os.Environ()+CGO_ENABLED=0 and GOFLAGS never stripped. Overlay keys are absolute paths under <root>/cmd/hband, so the working directory does not matter.

contracts.name: program.Start(t T, bin string, o Options) *Program

payload.coherence_check:
Two proposals, so the composition was checked at every seam where pieces come from different designers.

(1) Browser sign-in against the harness. Crossdomain's Visitor exposed SessionCookie for Network.setCookie. Practice's Chrome signs itself in. Shipping both would put two session paths into one test. Practice's was kept, so SessionCookie and Network.setCookie are removed. That also keeps the harness clear of the existing fitness rule that forbids http.Cookie literals in every .go file.

(2) Open(t) against crossdomain's Open(tb, browser). These are incompatible signatures. Open(t) was kept, so isEdge is not re-checked in Open: Browser already did it, and there is no path to re-check.

(3) Tags against helpers. Crossdomain's rule that a tag lies 'inside the named test's span' contradicts practice's DeepThread helper, which makes the seed assertions. The seam was redesigned: By may name any function, and a non-Test By must have a Via naming the test that runs it without a browser.

(4) Verbatim bodies against tags. Tagging the ten Go bodies would change their text away from the ledger, so Verbatim rows need no tags. An sha256-against-edition check was added in their place, which neither proposal had.

(5) Error semantics. unittest's stop-at-first-failure (Fatalf) and look()'s collect-then-fail (six Errorf) are both kept, each scoped to its own source, so one test does not mix the two contracts.

(6) Base URL. The HTTP tests use https://hband.test with :0, and the browser test uses loopback http with a picked port. The retry applies only in picked mode, and only to exit code 1, so line 4's exit-3 program is never retried into a pass.

(7) C5. Both proposals left it as uncommitted evidence. That conflicts with the rule that every case needs a check a machine runs unattended, so it was redesigned as a build-tagged committed test that reuses line 5's trigger technique.

(8) The narrow T in program against testing.TB in headless. They do not meet, because the launcher never opens a browser.

No decidable disagreement forces a re-synthesis. In-browser sign-in against setCookie is cheap: if it fails, one CDP verb is added and the build settles it. Whether the ten bodies already meet line 4 is handled inside this design by marked amendments. So decidable_disagreements is empty on purpose.

Nothing here has been contested on the contents of the six Python ledger bodies, because no designer and not this composition could read them. Their mapping rows are the builder's to write from the in-place SELECT, and the critique's to check against the recorded editions. The build-check survey should have quoted those assertions.

The stack block's '[testing] … --screenshot … Edge here … HBAND_TEST_BROWSER' line contradicts the measured headless.Browser (CHROME_BIN only) and Q-035, a person's decision to retire it. The measurement and the person agree; only the stack text is stale. This design builds to the measurement and declares the DevTools channel in stack_chosen.

The workaround-as-a-setting rule does not apply. Chrome's ~492 px window floor is stepped around inside test tooling by emulation, and nothing the app's user sees changes.

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: Legislative drafting: positive-law recodification, where scattered acts are re-enacted as one code and the old acts are then repealed
cross_domain_transfer.pattern: A recodification ships two tables. The disposition table says where every section of every old act went: carried over, omitted as obsolete, or superseded, each with a reason. The derivation table says which old section each new section came from. A 'no substantive change' rule holds unless an amendment is declared, and the repeal passes only when the disposition table is complete against a cited edition. Here the old acts are the six Python ledger bodies, the five tests/acceptance Python files and run_finish_e004_2.py. The sections are assertion sites. The disposition table is the rows. The derivation table is the `// ported:<ID>` tags. The cited edition is each source's sha256 or git blob. The repeal is SC-043.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: The slice is a repeal-without-loss problem: SC-043 deletes the Python on the strength of this mapping. Drafters solve exactly that with two tables that must reconcile and that survive the repeal, plus declared amendments, here the BROWSER RULE's change to the browser list, instead of silent omissions. The test-checked Go table is the mechanical form of both tables. Practice's mutation-testing transfer (PIT: killed, survived, no coverage) was also selected in part, as the breaks test's mark file, and is carried in prior_art.

invariants.precondition: Every provision of the old acts can be enumerated: each Python body's assertion sites can be identified.

The six ledger bodies were not read. The builder's first step is the in-place mode=ro SELECT. Per-source counts make an under-count visible to the critique.
